newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Holdings to stay in the limelight in Brussels.
newsitem.headline: Holdings to stay in the limelight in Brussels.

text.p: Holding companies are expected to bask in the limelight on the Brussels bourse in the next few months but will inevitably be stripped of the discount their shares offer relative to asset value, analysts said on Tuesday.
"Holdings will stay in the picture. It will be the story of the next few months," said Stefan Casteleyn at Corluy & Co.
Holding companies Gevaert, Almanij and Cobepa had been the star performers on Monday following a major reshuffle involving the three firms.
Casteleyn said fellow holdings like Belcofi and Ackermans were already taking over the baton.

Casteleyn, who already last year gave 'buy' recommendations for holdings in view of their undervaluation, said "the train would keep on running" until those companies were trading on a par with asset value or even at a premium.
"(Holding companies with large premiums) are clearly an endangered species," he said.

He said the moves by Almanij, Cobepa and Gevaert to simplify their structures to try and cut the discount had been remarkably late. Cobepa chief executive Pierre Scohier for one had been rallying against the large discount given by the market to his company.
Insurer Royale Belge, which thrived in recent sessions on speculation it might be sold by its French parent AXA-UAP, ended 0.4 percent lower at 9,900 francs.
Royale Belge is expected to reveal details on its future at its shareholders' meeting on Wednesday.

Kredietbank, which confirmed last week it was holding exploratory talks with Dutch co-operative bank Rabobank, is expected to rise further on merger speculation. It closed 0.7 percent higher at 14,500.
